name: dsm-b-matrix-multiply-add-on-lanes-zero-to-fifteen-loading-inside
rationale: Lanes 0-15 of one simdgroup of 32 load the fragments and run the multiply-add inside the branch; lanes 16-31 never load theirs, so the source defines no cell for them. Inputs (A): a is the row rotation a[r][(r + 4) & 7] = 1 (else 0), b[k][j] = 8k + j + 1, c[r][j] = 256 + 8r + j, so a whole simdgroup's d[r][j] = b[(r + 4) & 7][j] + c[r][j]: each result row is the b row four rows away, which another half of the simdgroup holds. Every cell, product, and sum is an integer below 2048, exact in float and half whatever the accumulation order. out[2g + j] is lane g's float cell j, out[2n + 2g + j] its half cell widened (n the grid's threads); a lane that does not run the multiply-add leaves its words at the 0xAB poison. The AIR has no loop.

name: dsm-b-matrix-multiply-add-on-lanes-zero-to-fifteen-loading-inside-other-inputs
rationale: dsm-b-matrix-multiply-add-on-lanes-zero-to-fifteen-loading-inside with input B. Inputs (B): a is the row rotation with a[r][(r + 4) & 7] = 2 where that column is 0, 1, 4, or 5 (the even lanes' columns) and 1 elsewhere, b[k][j] = 8k + j + 1 plus 64 in rows 4-7 (the cells lanes 16-31 hold), c[r][j] = 256 + 8r + j: input A with the even lanes' a cells and lanes 16-31's b cells changed. Every cell, product, and sum is an integer below 2048, exact in float and half whatever the accumulation order. out[2g + j] is lane g's float cell j, out[2n + 2g + j] its half cell widened (n the grid's threads); a lane that does not run the multiply-add leaves its words at the 0xAB poison. The AIR has no loop.

name: fragment-varying-float-to-half
rationale: The fragment entry truncates its perspective center scalar float varying to half and writes color location zero; the shared generated fullscreen vertex stage supplies the varying and the selected R16Float pixel captures the conversion byte-exactly.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-fourteen-dual-output
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 14 and receives exact float4 zero from all thirteen linked _uber_clear bodies. A sixteen-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. This entry swizzles it to float4(0,0,0,1), writes both required poisoned output textures, and captures binding zero byte-exactly.

name: kernel-stage-input-word
rationale: A uint3 stage-input record uses the product's padded 16-byte runtime-array stride; one thread copies its x lane into a poisoned output, proving the reflected synthetic buffer slot drives both Metal's stage-input descriptor and Vulkan's StorageBuffer binding.

name: lod-queries-of-2d-array-3d-cube-and-depth-textures
rationale: The LOD queries the AIR front end decodes, in a fragment function: a fullscreen draw into a 16x16 rgba32_float target (pre-filled with 0xAB; every fragment returns zero) where the fragment at (x, y) writes the clamped and unclamped LOD of eight textures to out[4(16y + x) .. 4(16y + x) + 3] of buffer 0 (float4 elements, pre-filled with 0xAB), through a runtime sampler (nearest, not mipmapped, clamp to edge, normalized). The coordinates are linear in the position: pos.xy / 16 (and 0.5 for the third 3D coordinate), and the cube direction (1, (8 - y) / 8, (8 - x) / 8) on the +X face, whose face coordinates are pos.xy / 16 too. Each texture's one level is a power-of-two multiple of 16 texels across, so its unclamped LOD is an exact integer: texture 0 2D array rgba16_float 64x64x2 (2), texture 1 3D 32x32x2 (1), texture 2 cube 32x32 (1), texture 3 cube array 16x16, 1 cube (0), texture 4 depth32_float 2D 32x32 (1), texture 5 depth 2D array 64x64x2 (2), texture 6 depth cube 8x8 (-1), texture 7 depth cube array 16x16, 1 cube (0); a one-level texture clamps every LOD to 0. The texels are never read. The AIR has no loop.

name: simd-sum-shuffle-shuffle-xor-and-ballot-in-a-vertex-function
rationale: Forty rasterization-disabled points; vertex v writes simd_sum, simd_shuffle from lane 5, simd_shuffle_xor by 1 and the ballot of in[v] > 0 (low and high words) to out[5v .. 5v + 4]. Metal runs simdgroup functions in a vertex function: on an M4 vertices 0 to 31 form one simdgroup and 32 to 39 another. The inputs are multiples of 1/8 with sums exact in any order. A device must support subgroup operations in the vertex stage; MoltenVK 1.4.1 does not list the vertex stage, and the translation refuses there, typed.

name: imageblock-word
rationale: One invocation initializes its explicit imageblock cell, reads it back, and writes 42 to a poisoned output buffer; 1x1 authored dimensions exercise the host allocation contract on Metal and the descriptor-free Workgroup lowering on Vulkan.

name: bicubic-at-four-texel-centres-of-three-array-slices
rationale:
Seventy-five corpus modules declare a bicubic sampler, and the lowering answers them with a hand-written sixteen-tap Catmull-Rom filter. Nothing had ever checked that against the hardware. The first question a bicubic emulation has to get right is which cubic family it is: an interpolating one returns the texel exactly at a texel centre, an approximating B-spline returns a blur of one sixth, two thirds, one sixth. This case asks the hardware that question.

The scale factor is one, so each of the four threads samples the centre of its own texel and both coordinate fractions are zero. The kernel loops over three array slices and writes the sampled red channel splatted across all four output channels, so the twelve observed halves are twelve source texels read back unchanged if and only if the filter interpolates. The source texels are sixty-fourths, which are exact halves, and each slice is offset so a slice mix-up is visible. The other three channels of each source texel hold different values so a channel swizzle is visible too.

Metal answers the texels exactly, so its filter::bicubic interpolates - the family the lowering picked. The companion case reads the weights themselves.

name: read-three-catmull-rom-weights-off-the-hardware-at-two-fractions
rationale:
The companion to the texel-centre bicubic case: this one reads Metal's cubic weights off the hardware one at a time instead of inferring the family.

Each source slice is zero everywhere except a single column of ones, and the column is constant down the whole height. A tap column that is constant in y makes the four y weights sum to exactly one, so the sampled value collapses to the single x weight at the tap that lands on the column - the shader reads out one filter coefficient as a number. The scale factor 5.5 puts the two threads at coordinate 2.25 and 7.75, so their fractions are a quarter and three quarters and their four-tap footprints, x=1..4 and x=6..9, do not overlap and do not reach an edge. The column position advances by one per array slice, so the three slices read the first three taps of each footprint.

Catmull-Rom with a = -1/2 predicts -9/128, 111/128 and 29/128 at a quarter and -3/128, 29/128 and 111/128 at three quarters. All six are exact halves, so the readout is byte-exact rather than approximate. Metal answers all six, which pins its filter::bicubic to the same cubic the lowering emits - including the negative lobes, which is what tells an interpolating cubic from a smoothing one.

name: extend-the-right-edge-of-a-three-tap-box-blur-past-the-destination-width
rationale:
A three-tap horizontal box blur over ARGB8 with edge-mode extend, 190 lines and one of 21 corpus hosts of `native/emitter/pointers/raw_select.rs::emit_raw_pointer_select_byte`, none of which had an authored case. The rule is the byte-granular twin of the word-granular pointer-select tail: thread zero picks the right-hand halo texel from either `&row[count]` or `&row[count - 1]` depending on whether the window runs past the source width, and both arms are raw byte offsets into the same device buffer, so the merged pointer is emitted as a select between two byte indices rather than between two pointers. The source is five pixels wide and the destination four, so `count + src_x_offset` is 4 and `src_width` is 5: the select takes its TRUE arm and reads pixel four, which no other output pixel reads and which differs from pixel three in three of its four channels. A select that picked the other arm would change the last destination pixel.

Every source channel is 0x00 or 0xFF, so every unpacked lane is exactly +0.0 or +1.0 and every window sums to 0, 1 or 2 -- exact in half and independent of the order the three addends are combined in, which is what makes the answer association-proof under `fast` math. The channel patterns are chosen so no window ever sums to 3, whose product with the literal 1/3 (`0xH3555`, 0.333251953125) lands exactly on a half rounding tie. The two products that do occur, 0.333251953125 and 0.66650390625, are exact halves and pack to 0x55 and 0xAA with no tie either. Every params byte outside the seven fields the kernel loads is 0xCC, including `background_color`, which this edge mode never reads. `loop_free`: the entry has no back edge.

name: linked-single-threadgroup-zero-bin
rationale: One 1x1 threadgroup dispatches one invocation. kLogBinEntries=0 makes both initialization and flush loops contain exactly one bin, kTGSizeIs256=false uses the literal one-thread group size as their stride, and source_size=1x1 bounds the image path. The exact linked callback returns float4 zero without dereferencing resources; the poisoned global bin makes the local-atomic aggregation observable byte-exactly.

name: linked-k24-quantized-vector-matrix
rationale: Reaching variant of linked-zero-k cases of this entry, whose parameters stop the kernel before its arithmetic. One threadgroup of 32 lanes; the user constant keeps 8-bit unsigned weights, group size one, no bias; constant 122 binds a two-entry table (1 source, 1 destination). The parameters select N = 32 outputs (one threadgroup's 32 columns) over K = 24 rows: the guard (threadgroup_position.y << 5) < N passes, lanes 0 to 23 each dequantize one 8-bit row of W (row stride N bytes) and scale it, the simdgroup sums the 32 partial results, and lane 0 hands all 32 to the linked destination callback, which writes table entry 1 at element indices 0 to 31 (128 bytes, observed whole). x holds 1, 2, 3 repeating, the scales 0.5, 1, 2 repeating, the biases 0 to 3 repeating, and W small integers below 16, so every product and partial sum is an integer multiple of 0.5 far below 2^24: exact in any order or contraction.

name: linked-zero-k-quantized-vector-matrix
no_effect: The authored parameters give the work an empty extent, so the entry returns before any write reaches the selected output.
rationale: One invocation uses a one-element linked destination array. The authored user constant selects eight-bit quantization, group size one, and zero vector rows; the exact zero K parameter makes both accumulation counts zero. Every arithmetic loop and the final postfix loop is therefore zero-trip, so the poisoned linked destination remains byte-exact while the wrapper and linkage contract execute. Replaced: the linked destination callback writes table entry 1, so the case binds a two-entry table (MPSNDArrayRefSize 1 source, 1 destination) whose destination element carries the source element's fill.

name: relaxed-atomic-load-of-a-device-limit
rationale: Eight threads read the device atomic limit n = 5 with a relaxed atomic load, its only access (access.atomic.buffer.load), and write out[i] = a[i] for i < 5 and 1000 + n = 1005 otherwise, where a[i] = 100 + 7i: (100, 107, 114, 121, 128, 1005, 1005, 1005). No thread stores the atomic, so every load reads 5. The AIR has no loop.

name: linked-single-lane-mx-dequantize
no_effect: The linked destination callback is a no-op by design, so the destination element keeps its authored bytes while the dequantization path runs.
rationale: One invocation reads exactly four packed quantized bytes and one shared scale byte from the two authored device-array inputs. The exact linked primary float4 destination is the retained no-op callback; the sole poisoned destination element therefore remains byte-exact and proves the linked callback contract while the dequantization path executes.

name: sixteen-lanes-dequantize-through-the-public-linked-destination
rationale: Reaching variant of the single-lane case of this entry, whose linked destination callback was the retained postfixPrimary_4xf, which writes nothing. This case links the public module validation/fixtures/public/linked/mps_postfix_primary_4xf_to_last_buffer (owned MSL): it stores the float4 at elements coordinate.x to coordinate.x + 3 of the kernel's buffer table's last array (constant 122 = 3 gives the kernel three arrays, and the callback the count 3), so each dequantized value reaches the destination. Sixteen threads (one threadgroup) each read 2 packed bytes of FP4 E2M1 nibbles at 2 * gid.x from array 0 and one scale byte at (4 gid.x) >> 4 from array 1 (FP8 E4M3 scales 0x38 (1), 0xc4 (-3), 0x31 (0.5625), 0x4a (5), one per 16 elements); thread gid.x writes elements 4 gid.x to 4 gid.x + 3 of array 2 (256 bytes, poisoned 0xab before), so every thread's four words are observed and none overlaps another's. The codes spread over the format's nonzero finite encodings (no zero of either sign, whose sign the kernels' fast math leaves unspecified, and no NaN or infinity); every decoded value times its scale is a normal float, exact, 50 distinct words. Straight-line code: no loop.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-ten-dual-output

name: merge-two-descriptors-at-a-phi-and-index-both-arms
rationale: A device pointer merged across TWO DESCRIPTORS by a phi, twice, with the two merges taking opposite arms. Logical SPIR-V has no value that can be either descriptor, so the translator lowers each merge to a PhysicalStorageBuffer64 device address: it synthesizes an address table, loads each buffer's address from it, phis between the two ADDRESSES, and turns every index off a merged pointer into a physical access chain. Coverage, measured rather than assumed: this is the SECOND case to reach construct_interface_cross_binding_pointer_phis_module, not the first -- irreducible-pointer-phi-rebuild-observed-at-arm-2 already does. Compared against it under llvm-cov, this module reaches no psb/pointer FUNCTION that case misses (it misses 18 that case reaches), and takes five branches inside psb_value_select's discover_value_selects, rewrite_cross_binding_pointer_merges_to_values and phi_suffix_indices_dominate_predecessors, plus one in Emitter::pointer_meta_for_value, that it does not. What it adds semantically is the shape that case has no room for: TWO merges over the SAME descriptor pair with opposite arms, and an index re-derived off one of them at a second dynamic offset. a holds 100+i and b holds 200+i, so the arm each merge chose is legible in the output word itself. p takes a on lanes 0-3 and b on lanes 4-7; q takes the other one; the third row reads p again at 7-gid, so a merge re-derived per use rather than carried has to agree with itself. All 24 expected words are distinct: out[0..7]=100 101 102 103 204 205 206 207, out[8..15]=200 201 202 203 104 105 106 107, out[16..23]=107 106 105 104 203 202 201 200. A swapped arm turns the first row into the second; a merge that collapses to one descriptor makes rows one and two equal; a leak between p and q swaps them on one half of the grid; and an index recomputed from the wrong merge puts b's words in the third row's low lanes. Every value is an exact small integer, so nothing here depends on rounding or on association.
